title: Performance budgets and performance regression in the pipeline

videos.script: Performance rarely breaks in one release. It leaks. {{leak}} A library here, a bigger picture there, a query that lost its index in a migration nobody reviewed closely. Each change costs a few milliseconds, and each one passes, because nobody measured. {{drift}} Six months later the page takes four seconds and nobody can say which change did it. {{blame}} The fix is to measure on every change, and to let a program decide. That needs three things. {{three}} A budget for the page, written down before anyone argues about it. {{budget}} A baseline for the server, so a regression shows up even while it is still under the requirement. {{baseline}} And enough runs to tell a real slowdown from a noisy machine, because one run is a sample, not a verdict. {{noise}} By the end of this lesson those three are one shell script. It fails on the slow page from lesson 10, passes on the fixed one, and fails again the moment the database loses its index. {{gate}} A pipeline only has to read its exit code. {{pipeline}}
